account:
It is just after eight on Day 1, and I am in my office with the secretary nearby for scheduled business. I read today's appointments and returned the books to the appointments chest. My day includes a ten o'clock grain inspection at the east-bank mill, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen hundred, tea with the neighbour at fifteen hundred, office time at sixteen-thirty, and the innkeeper's community gathering in the great hall at eighteen hundred before going home at nineteen hundred. The gathering is an addition I approved yesterday; the innkeeper also wanted a private catering discussion with the secretary, which appears to concern its arrangements. I do not know what they discussed privately.

The only unusual report I know of is a vague mention of a bridge or port change that the neighbour heard near the bakery. There is no identified firsthand source or confirmed proposal. The secretary found nothing about it in the office records checked, but that does not rule out records elsewhere. I asked for discreet enquiries near the bakery rather than spreading it as fact. I cannot yet say who, if anyone, is pursuing such a change or what it is for.

We are also trying to locate the town accounts ledger and incoming council correspondence. The secretary's written report did not establish either location or the ledger's keeper. This morning I checked the treasury: it contained two stacks of sixty-four emeralds, but no ledger or letters. I left the money untouched. Apart from these unanswered administrative questions, I have seen no confirmed disruption in town.
